Definition: Stock symbol, for example 'KO'.
Sector name, used to compare a stock with its peers.
Coverage Notes: Join key to the sector table. In Assignment 5 the loader wrote 'Realestate' instead of 'Real Estate', so check that the names match exactly.

Definition: Date of the data snapshot a row describes.
Forward annual dividend per share, in dollars. Blank for non-payers.
Coverage Notes: Verified on 49 tickers: blank (not 0) for all 8 non-payers, present for all 41 payers. A blank means no dividend.

Definition: Forward dividend yield: dividend_rate divided by share price. Yahoo's dividendYield is a percent (3.0 means 3%), so divide by 100 to store a fraction.
Coverage Notes: Verified: dividendYield divided by (dividendRate / price) was 91 to 101 for every payer, so it is a percent. Returns 0, not blank, for non-payers. The forward yield is our main yield measure.

Definition: Dividends paid over the last 12 months divided by price. A fraction, but UNRELIABLE (see Coverage Notes). Use dividend_yield instead.
Coverage Notes: Unreliable: for MCD, HD, CAT, and NVDA the trailing annual dividend rate is only 23% to 50% of the forward dividendRate (MCD 1.86 versus 7.72), so the trailing yield is understated. Do not use in scores.

Definition: Dividends per share paid over the last 12 months. DROPPED: it is understated for MCD, HD, CAT, and NVDA, so it is listed here only so nobody adds it later without knowing.
Coverage Notes: Only 23% to 50% of the forward dividendRate for MCD, HD, CAT, and NVDA (MCD 1.86 versus 7.72).

Definition: Average yield over five years, used as a baseline for the current yield. A percent (3.0 means 3%), so divide by 100.
Coverage Notes: Present for 40 of 41 payers (97.6%). GOOGL is missing, probably because it began paying recently. The median value is 2.69, which confirms percent units.

Definition: dividend_yield divided by five_year_avg_dividend_yield. A value well above 1 can mean the price fell on bad news, not that the income improved. Convert both inputs to the same unit first. Undefined when the five-year average is missing.
Coverage Notes: Cannot be computed for GOOGL (no five-year average) or for non-payers.

Definition: Share of earnings paid out as dividends. Above 1.0 means the company pays out more than it earns. A fraction (0.5 means 50%). Not meaningful for REITs, whose accounting earnings are low.
Coverage Notes: Present for all payers (0, not blank, for non-payers). Above 1.0 for ABBV (1.17), PFE (2.46), UPS (1.26), and the REIT O (2.22).

Definition: Most recent ex-dividend date. Yahoo returns a Unix timestamp in seconds (1796083200 is 1 December 2026), which has to be converted to a date.
Coverage Notes: Present for 44 of 49 tickers: all 41 payers plus 3 former payers with old dates (AMD 1995, BA 2020, INTC 2024). Do not use it to detect payers.

Definition: Number of shares outstanding, used to turn the per-share dividend into a total dividend bill.
Coverage Notes: Present for all 49 tickers.

Definition: free_cashflow divided by total dividends (dividend_rate times shares_outstanding). Below 1 means free cash flow does not cover the dividend. Can be computed only when free_cashflow is present, and is negative when free cash flow is negative.
Coverage Notes: Depends on free_cashflow, which is missing for 8 payers (MCD, CVX, PFE, JPM, BAC, WFC, GS, BLK) and negative for DUK, SO, NEE, and GOOGL. Sector exceptions TBD.

Definition: Consecutive years the annual dividend increased, counted from the dividend history. Stretch goal.
Coverage Notes: Not tested. Needs the dividend history, not the info fields.

Definition: Sensitivity to market moves. Above 1 means the stock swings more than the market.
Coverage Notes: Present for 40 of 41 payers (97.6%) and 48 of 49 tickers overall. Only MCD is missing.

Definition: Annualized standard deviation of daily returns over the last 252 trading days (daily standard deviation times the square root of 252). Needs a price-history backfill.
Coverage Notes: Not covered by the coverage check, which only tests Yahoo info fields. Needs one year of price history.

Definition: Largest peak-to-trough fall in closing price over the last year, as a negative fraction.
Coverage Notes: Not covered by the coverage check. Needs one year of price history.

Definition: Total debt relative to shareholder equity (leverage). Yahoo's value is percent-style (71 means 0.71), so divide by 100 for a plain ratio. Often missing for banks.
Coverage Notes: Present for 34 of 41 payers (82.9%). Missing: MCD, PM, MO, ABBV, JPM, BAC, WFC. Extreme values: GS 756 (7.56x) and AMT 464 (4.64x), so cap outliers.

Definition: Current assets divided by current liabilities: the ability to cover short-term bills.
Coverage Notes: Present for 34 of 41 payers (82.9%). Missing: MCD, CVX, PFE, JPM, BAC, WFC, BLK. Outlier: VICI at 20.3.

Definition: Operating cash flow minus capital spending, in dollars. This is raw dollars, which favors big companies, so scores should use fcf_dividend_coverage.
Coverage Notes: Present for 33 of 41 payers (80.5%). Missing: MCD, CVX, PFE, JPM, BAC, WFC, GS, BLK. Negative for DUK, SO, NEE, and GOOGL.

Definition: Overall governance risk score published by Yahoo, on a 1 to 10 scale. Higher is probably riskier, but confirm against Yahoo's definition before using it.
Coverage Notes: Present for all 49 tickers, range 1 to 10. TSLA, BRK-B, and GOOGL all score 10, which hints that 10 is riskiest. The direction is not yet confirmed. Four sub-scores (audit, board, compensation, shareholder rights) are also present for every ticker but are not in this dictionary.

Definition: Price divided by earnings per share over the trailing 12 months (TTM). Negative or missing means no profits.
Coverage Notes: Present for 48 of 49 tickers. INTC is missing (negative earnings). Extreme value: TSLA at 375, so cap outliers.

Definition: Price divided by expected earnings for the next 12 months.
Coverage Notes: Present for all 49 tickers. The maximum is 158, so cap outliers.

Definition: 1 if dividend_rate is present and greater than 0, else 0. A blank dividend_rate means non-payer. Do not use the yield or payout columns (0 for non-payers) or ex_dividend_date (old dates for former payers) to decide.
Coverage Notes: Verified: dividendRate is blank for all 8 non-payers in the sample.

Definition: 1 if payout_ratio is between 0 and 1 (earnings cover the dividend), else 0. The threshold is the team's decision. Sector exceptions are TBD, because REITs report low accounting earnings.
Coverage Notes: Would fail ABBV, PFE, UPS, and the REIT O in the sample.

Definition: 1 if free_cashflow is greater than 0, else 0. Sector exceptions are TBD.
Coverage Notes: Would fail the utilities DUK, SO, NEE, and GOOGL. Cannot be evaluated for the 8 payers with no free cash flow.

Definition: 1 if fcf_dividend_coverage is at least 1, else 0. Sector exceptions are TBD.
Coverage Notes: Cannot be evaluated when free cash flow is missing. Negative for DUK, SO, NEE, and GOOGL.

Definition: 1 if every field needed for the score is present and plausible, else 0. Missing values are excluded, never filled with 0. The list of required fields is TBD.
Coverage Notes: In the sample, 11 of 41 payers are missing at least one of beta, debt-to-equity, current ratio, or free cash flow.

Definition: Sum of the flag fields. The pass cutoff is the team's decision (the Deep Value example kept stocks scoring 5 or more out of 9).
Z-score, within the stock's sector, of winsorized volatility_1y (1st and 99th percentile, also within the sector), inverted so a higher z means lower risk.
Coverage Notes: Needs enough stocks per sector to be meaningful. The 49-ticker sample has only 3 utilities, so score the full S&P 500.

Definition: Z-score, within the stock's sector, of winsorized beta (1st and 99th percentile, also within the sector), inverted so a higher z means lower risk.
Z-score, within the stock's sector, of winsorized debt_to_equity (1st and 99th percentile, also within the sector), inverted so a higher z means lower leverage.
Coverage Notes: Missing for many financials, so those stocks are scored on their other metrics.

Definition: Z-score, within the stock's sector, of winsorized dividend_yield (1st and 99th percentile, also within the sector), not inverted.
Z-score, within the stock's sector, of winsorized fcf_dividend_coverage (1st and 99th percentile, also within the sector), not inverted.
Coverage Notes: Missing for financials. Utilities have negative values, which is why scoring is within the sector.

Definition: Weighted sum of the available safety z-scores (z_volatility, z_beta, z_debt_to_equity). A stock missing a metric is scored on the metrics it has and flagged with partial_data. Weights are the team's decision (TBD).

Weighted sum of the available income z-scores (z_dividend_yield, z_fcf_coverage). A stock missing a metric is scored on the metrics it has and flagged with partial_data. Weights are the team's decision (TBD).

Low, Medium, or High, from cutoffs on safety_composite within each sector (for example the top third of a sector is Low). Low means safest among sector peers, not safe in absolute terms. The cutoffs are the team's decision (TBD).
The stock's rank within its sector by safety_composite (1 is the safest in its sector). Shown to the user next to risk_level.
1 if the stock was scored with fewer than all of its metrics, else 0, so the agent can tell the user the score used partial data.
Coverage Notes: Expect a meaningful share of stocks to be flagged: financials lack free cash flow data and several stocks lack debt-to-equity.

Definition: Low, Medium, or High, chosen by the user and matched against risk_level.
Google GenAI SDK client (genai.Client()) used to call Gemini. The API key is read from an environment variable and never stored in code or the repo.
Gemini model identifier. The class example uses 'gemini-2.5-flash'; confirm the model with the professor.
Gemini's explanation of the top-ranked stocks. It may use only the numbers passed in from the database and must not supply figures of its own.
